idiom_name: async fn / Future + executor, with the Waker as the completion notification
implementation_notes: Rust models completion rather than events: an async fn returns a Future whose poll the executor calls, and when the operation finishes the Waker stored in the Context 'notifies [the] executor that [the task] is ready to be run', which re-polls it and resumes the awaiting task - the completion callback is the waker. Start-now means spawning the future (tokio::spawn returns a JoinHandle) or holding it in an already-running task, and success, failure and cancellation are ordinary values (Result, drop), so no AsyncCompletedEventArgs-shaped payload is needed. Wrap foreign callback APIs once, with a oneshot channel or a hand-written Future, and keep the async surface everywhere else.
pitfalls: Futures are inert: constructing one starts nothing until it is awaited or spawned, so an unawaited future silently never runs.
Blocking inside an async task (std::thread::sleep, blocking I/O) starves the runtime worker - move it to spawn_blocking or a dedicated thread.
Dropping the JoinHandle detaches the task, and a task that panics yields JoinError with its result lost; cancellation by dropping is silent unless the API reports it.
